ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 mins

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 1 tbsp butter. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Add tomato puree, cumin powder, coriander powder, 1 tsp red chili powder, and sugar to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the oil starts to separate from the mixture. Add the soaked cashews and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a simmer.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if desired, for a smoother gravy). Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. If the gravy is too thick, add a little more water. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an ultra-smooth consistency.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Add 1 tbsp butter and the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the gravy. Stir in the fresh cream just before serving. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice. Enjoy your homemade Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani!

tips: For a truly authentic taste, lightly toast the kasoori methi in a dry pan for a minute before crushing it into the gravy.
If you dont have fresh tomatoes, good quality canned crushed tomatoes or tomato passata work wonderfully for the gravy base.
Always add fresh cream at the very end of cooking and avoid boiling the gravy afterward to prevent it from splitting or curdling.
article:
Mastering the Art of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: Your Ultimate Indian Lunch Guide

There are few dishes in the culinary world that evoke such universal delight as Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian curry, with its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce and succulent pieces of chicken, has captivated palates across the globe. Whether you’re a seasoned cook or a kitchen novice, learning to prepare this beloved dish at home is a rewarding experience that promises to bring the vibrant flavors of India right to your dining table. Perfect for a hearty lunch or an elegant dinner, this Butter Chicken Recipe is a staple for a reason. Let's delve into everything you need to know to create this masterpiece.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s at the famous Moti Mahal restaurant, it was created by Kundan Lal Jaggi and Kundan Lal Gujral. They sought to use leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich, velvety tomato and butter gravy. The result was a culinary sensation that quickly spread, becoming one of the most recognizable and cherished Indian dishes worldwide.

At its heart, Murgh Makhani is characterized by its tender chicken pieces (often pre-marinated and grilled or pan-fried) swimming in a luxurious sauce. This sauce is a harmonious blend of pureed tomatoes, fresh cream, generous amounts of butter, and a delicate balance of aromatic spices like ginger, garlic, garam masala, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Unlike many other Indian curries, Butter Chicken is typically mild, leaning towards sweet and tangy notes rather than intense heat, making it incredibly appealing to a wide range of palates, including children. It's the ultimate comfort food, offering a symphony of textures and flavors that are both comforting and exquisitely decadent.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken Recipe requires a combination of fresh ingredients and essential spices. Here’s what you’ll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   **Chicken:** 750g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces. Thighs are recommended for juiciness.
*   **Plain Yogurt:** 1/2 cup, full-fat.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Kashmiri Red Chili Powder:** 1 teaspoon (for color, mild heat).
*   **Turmeric Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon.
*   **Cumin Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon.
*   **Garam Masala:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Salt:** 1 teaspoon, or to taste.

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   **Ghee or Unsalted Butter:** 2 tablespoons ghee or 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus extra for finishing.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Green Cardamom Pods:** 3-4, lightly crushed.
*   **Cinnamon Stick:** 1 small (about 1-inch).
*   **Bay Leaf:** 1.
*   **Tomato Puree/Crushed Tomatoes:** 1 can (400g/14oz) high-quality crushed tomatoes, or 3-4 large ripe tomatoes pureed.
*   **Cashew Paste:** 1/4 cup raw cashews soaked in hot water for 15 minutes, then blended into a smooth paste with a little water. This adds richness and thickness.
*   **Kashmiri Red Chili Powder:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Garam Masala:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Sugar:** 1-2 teaspoons, or to taste (balances acidity).
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Water or Chicken Broth:** 1/2 to 1 cup, as needed for consistency.
*   **Fresh Cream (Heavy Cream):** 1/2 cup, plus extra for garnish.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** 1-2 teaspoons, crushed between your palms (essential for authentic flavor).
*   **Fresh Coriander:** For garnish, chopped.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Butter Chicken Recipe:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee or oil in a large skillet or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is lightly browned on all sides and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes per batch. Set the cooked chicken aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan (add more ghee/butter if needed), reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining ghee or butter. Once melted, add the cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4.  **Sauté Aromatics:** Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
5.  **Build the Tomato Base:** Pour in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add Kashmiri red chili powder, garam masala, sugar, and salt. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate from the edges. This step is crucial for developing deep tomato flavor.
6.  **Add Cashew Paste & Simmer:** Stir in the cashew paste and 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Bring back to a simmer and cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken further.
7.  **Blend (Optional but Recommended):** For an ultra-smooth restaurant-style sauce, carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (remove bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods if you prefer) and blend until completely smooth. Pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an even silkier texture.
8.  **Finish the Sauce:** Return the pan to low heat. Stir in the fresh cream and crushed kasoori methi. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Gently simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the sauce.
9.  **Serve:** Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Stir in an extra knob of butter right before serving for that signature richness. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander and a swirl of extra cream.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, mouth-watering Butter Chicken Recipe takes a little finesse. Here are some expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skip the marination step. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **High-Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or very ripe fresh tomatoes. They form the backbone of your sauce.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** It’s called Butter Chicken for a reason! These ingredients provide the signature richness and velvety texture. Use full-fat dairy for the best results.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves impart a unique, slightly bitter, and sweet aroma that is characteristic of Murgh Makhani. Don't omit it. Crush it between your palms before adding to release its full fragrance.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** The sauce should be a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Adjust sugar and salt to your preference. A pinch of sugar helps cut the acidity of the tomatoes.
*   **Blend for Smoothness:** For that silky, restaurant-style texture, blending and straining the sauce is a game-changer.
*   **Don't Overcook the Chicken:** Cook the chicken just until done before adding it to the sauce. It will continue to cook slightly in the sauce, so you want to avoid it becoming dry.
*   **Low and Slow Simmer:** After adding the cream, keep the heat low and simmer gently. High heat can cause the cream to split.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with the right accompaniments.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan is the classic choice, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience further.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera (cumin) rice provides a neutral base that beautifully complements the curry's complex flavors.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads like whole wheat roti or flaky paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Cucumber Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based side dish with grated cucumber and spices provides a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Simple Salad:** A fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette can add a nice crunch and balance to the meal.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional Butter Chicken Recipe is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to your dietary needs or preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Makhani:** Easily transform this into Paneer Makhani by substituting chicken with cubed paneer (Indian cottage cheese), which can be lightly fried before adding to the sauce. Tofu or chickpeas can also be used for a plant-based version.
*   **Spice Level:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the sauce along with the ginger-garlic paste.
*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can also use Greek yogurt in the marinade for extra tang and protein. Cooking the chicken in an air fryer or oven instead of pan-frying can also reduce oil.
*   **Nut-Free Option:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute the cashew paste with an equal amount of melon seed paste (magaj) or skip it entirely and rely on a bit more cream or a spoonful of cornstarch slurry for thickness.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic tandoor-like smoky flavor, after the chicken is cooked, you can do a quick "dhungar" (smoking) method by placing a small bowl with a hot piece of charcoal in the chicken pot, drizzling a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly covering the pot for a few minutes.

Creating your own Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just cooking; it's an experience in rich flavors and aromatic spices. This detailed Butter Chicken Recipe provides all the guidance you need to prepare a dish that's sure to impress and satisfy, making any lunch or dinner feel like a special occasion. Enjoy the journey of making this iconic Indian delicacy!
